newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian religious leaders to work for harmony.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian religious leaders to work for harmony.

text.p: Religious leaders in an Indonesian town hit by violence in which at least five people died in church burnings have pledged to work for religious harmony, the Jakarta Post daily reported on Saturday.
The pledge was made by local Moslem, Catholic, Protestant and Hindu leaders in the East Java town of Situbondo on Friday, the paper said.

On October 10 a Moslem mob burned 24 churches and a Hindu temple in Situbondo after it heard that the defendant in a court hearing into alleged blasphemy against Islam had escaped and taken sanctuary in a church.
"We regret the October 10 incident in Situbondo," a joint statement from the religious leaders said.
"We appeal to the government and the public to contain the problem so it does not spread to other areas," it said.

"We appeal to the government and the public for restraint (and)...we hope religious and community leaders will work hand in hand and shoulder to shoulder to foster peaceful coexistence between religious communities."

The report quoted Situbondo regency chief Soedarjanto as estimating material losses from the incident at 4.8 billion rupiah ($2 million). Shops, cars and government buildings were damaged in the hours before security forces regained control.
The military has said it suspected an unidentified group was behind the riot.
Police said five people, including a pastor and his wife, were burnt to death in one church.
Church sources said a sixth person died in the attacks.
Indonesia, where religious tolerance is part of the state ideology, is the world's largest Moslem nation with around 85 percent of its population of more than 195 million followers of Islam.
